articles.title: Clice v1.0 Released: Welcome to Modern C++
articles.content: clice recently hit 1,000 commits, a special milestone for the project. Since July 19, 2026, clice has been shipping nightly builds and going through roughly four months of alpha testing, with a huge number of bugs fixed thanks to real-world feedback from early users. Over the same stretch, I built a rigorous testing system for clice and ran extensive tests across many real open-source projects, tracking down and fixing the issues they uncovered. What does that mean? Every core feature is now stable, and you rarely run into problems in day-to-day use. So I think the time is right to ship the first stable release. The project looks very different today from where it stood two years ago in Design and Implementation of a New C++ Language Server , and this is probably the first time I’m promoting it widely, so please let me introduce it to you once again! This is the project I have poured the past two and a half years into, the work I am proudest of, the one that has excited me the most and left me sad and anxious more times than I can count, and the most ambitious thing I have taken on in my short life. What is clice? In short, clice is a C/C++ language server written in modern C++ , but it’s more than just a language server. It is still built on LLVM/Clang, but unlike clangd and ccls, which are also Clang-based, clice was redesigned from the ground up to fix architectural problems that have gone unsolved in those servers for years. It is written entirely in C++23 and serves as an example of modern C++ best practices in its own right, with all the major modern C++ features coming together remarkably well: Written entirely with C++20 coroutines , using our own libuv-based structured-concurrency async library for intricate asynchronous logic. It is a complex concurrent program running an event loop on the main thread while coordinating both multiple processes (IPC) and multiple threads. Written entirely with C++20 named modules and C++23 import std , and fully self-hosted: module wrappers for third-party libraries are generated automatically by clice modularize , and clice runs smoothly on its own codebase to provide module-aware language services. Uses static reflection built on templates and C++20 concepts for all serialization and deserialization across formats, including TOML, JSON, bincode, blob, and command-line arguments, with Rust-macro-like declarative annotations and zero boilerplate. Data-oriented code design throughout, with almost no virtual functions outside the callback interfaces Clang requires. Makes heavy use of modern C++ APIs like std::format , std::expected , std::ranges , and std::views , steering clear of outdated legacy C++98/11 APIs. A completely hermetic, reproducible build powered by Bazel, compiled with the unified xclang toolchain for a consistent cross-platform cross-compilation workflow. Compiled binaries are heavily optimized (PGO + LTO), and build artifacts depend on nothing beyond system libraries. People are always de
articles.summary: C++ 工具项目 clice 发布 v1.0，历经约四个月 alpha 测试和大量真实反馈修复，正式进入现代 C++ 开发场景。

articles.title: Vulcan rocket fails during return-to-flight launch, 40 Amazon satellites lost
articles.content: Follow us Add us as a preferred source on Google Newsletter Subscribe to our newsletter United Launch Alliance's Vulcan Centaur rocket suffered an anomaly during its launch today (Nov. 15), resulting in the loss of 40 Amazon internet satellites. The Vulcan Centaur lifted off from Florida's Cape Canaveral Space Force Station today at 12:40 p.m. ET (1740 GMT), hauling 40 satellites for the Amazon Leo broadband constellation toward low Earth orbit (LEO). But they never got there. "Based on data received by our Launch Director, we confirm that the Vulcan vehicle launched from Space Launch Complex 41 suffered an anomaly 10 minutes into the flight and failed to deliver the Amazon mission to orbit," ULA said in an update on X today , 50 minutes after launch. "Since the anomaly just occurred, we don’t have any specific data yet to understand what occurred today." A United Launch Alliance Vulcan Centaur launches 40 Amazon internet satellites from Florida on Nov. 15, 2026. (Image credit: ULA) Today's launch was supposed to be a bounce-back mission for the Vulcan Centaur, the successor to ULA's workhorse Atlas V rocket. Vulcan debuted in January 2024 and had four total flights under its belt before today. On two of those missions — its second, in October 2024 , and its fourth, in February of this year — the rocket experienced an issue with one of its solid rocket boosters (SRBs). In both cases, an SRB nozzle burned through and fell off about 30 seconds after launch. Vulcan Centaur overcame the problem on both launches, successfully delivering its payloads to their designated orbits. But the U.S. Space Force was concerned enough that it decided to pause national security launches on Vulcan until ULA addressed the problem. (Vulcan's third and fourth launches were Space Force missions.) ULA worked hard on that front and got Vulcan ready to return to flight, which finally occurred today after nine months.. "The integrated team has made great strides in improving our understanding of the SRB anomaly that occurred on the previous Vulcan flight and have identified several potential contributors, which have been mitigated through design and process improvements to the nozzle," the company said in an Oct. 28 update . That nozzle work apparently paid off: The SRBs appeared to perform as expected during today's launch. But a different, more serious problem cropped up today, and Vulcan Centaur could not overcome it. The Vulcan Centaur rises into the sky on Nov. 15, 2026. (Image credit: Vulcan Centaur) Today's launch was supposed to help build out Amazon's broadband constellation in LEO, which was previously called Project Kuiper but is now known as Amazon Leo. It will eventually compete with SpaceX's Starlink network, which has been up and running for several years. Amazon Leo will consist of more than 3,200 satellites. Before today, about 400 of them had reached space on 15 launches, which were conducted by three different rockets — the Atlas V, SpaceX's Falcon 9 and

articles.title: Old Bitly links are being hijacked
articles.content: Update, 15 November, 23:40 UTC: CNN reports redirected Bitly links in old posts from Bill Gates, Justin Trudeau, Mike Pence, the FBI and the US Department of Defense as well. Our third check of the Trump links, at 23:35 UTC, found nothing new: 49 links re-created years after their tweets still work. Update, 15 November, 22:30 UTC: Bitly has confirmed the problem. In a post on X at 19:13 UTC it said it had identified an issue that “allowed bad actors to repurpose certain old, inactive links” and send people to unrelated content. Bitly said it has suspended the accounts involved and is disabling the affected links. It added that its Trust and Safety team is working on protections against similar misuse. Update, 15 November, 19:30 UTC: The Burger King and McDonald’s links no longer redirect. Both were still working at 15:05 UTC and returned Bitly’s “Link Deactivated” page by 19:22 UTC. The same has happened to the two extra Trump links we verified and to six of the seven links in our sample that pointed somewhere new. The seventh now shows a Bitly warning that the account that created it has been suspended. The 49 re-created links that look like the originals still work. Burger King’s X account was not hacked. A Bitly short link in a tweet the chain posted on 24 July 2011 was registered again by someone else on 15 November 2026 and pointed at Wikipedia’s list of Nazi concentration camps. The tweet was advertising a restaurant locator. A post quoting it passed 2 million views within hours, and Burger King’s original has since become unavailable. It was not the only one. Eighteen minutes earlier a Bitly link in a McDonald’s tweet from 7 June 2011 was registered the same way and pointed at Wikipedia’s article on the September 11 attacks. Ransomnews also checked 97 Bitly links in Donald Trump’s tweets from 2009 to 2013, taken from a public archive. Bitly’s own link pages show that 56 were created after the tweets they sit in, and a 57th is blocked by Bitly as malicious or spam. Four were registered on 15 November. Two more, created in January 2024 and January 2025, point at domains that copy the names of crypto services. In brief Burger King posted the tweet on 24 July 2011 with the short link bit[.]ly/19BFiM. Bitly’s information page for that link gives a creation time of 05:32 UTC on 15 November 2026 and a destination on Wikipedia. A link in a McDonald’s tweet from 7 June 2011, bit[.]ly/mLWJO0, was created again at 05:14 UTC the same morning, 18 minutes before Burger King’s. It opens Wikipedia’s article on the September 11 attacks. Both tweets have since become unavailable. Nobody posted from either company’s account. The links changed hands on Bitly’s side, so the old tweets send readers wherever the new owners choose. Of 97 Bitly links in Donald Trump’s tweets from 2009 to 2013, 40 are still the original. Another 49 were created again later but lead where the tweets suggest, 48 of them in a 17-minute run on 26 May 2023. Seven lead somewhere else and
articles.summary: 旧 Bitly 短链接遭劫持，被重定向至其他内容，涉及盖茨、特鲁多、FBI 等账号历史帖子，引发链接安全担忧。

articles.title: Protomaps: Self-hosting map tiles has gotten cheap and easy
articles.content: PMTiles is a tile format which works via HTTP Range requests and can be deployed as a single file to a storage bucket. I came across Protomaps in research for my latest project, Mapboard . 1 For most non-commercial projects, commercial APIs become prohibitively expensive if you ever go viral (Mapbox, for instance, charges $5 per 1k map loads once you’ve exhausted the free tier). PMTiles, part of the Protomaps ecosystem, is a tile format that ships in a single file, accessible via Range requests, and is thus extremely portable and easy to deploy. For CDNs that support caching Range requests of large files, it requires no effort besides down- and uploading it to storage. For others, like Cloudflare, you can utilize an edge function to translate between the traditional x/y/z URL path and Range requests. Getting some Maps If all you want is the world map, getting it is as simple as going to the build page and downloading the latest daily build. However, more fun can be had with the CLI . For example, you can extract data for only a bounding box or specific zoom levels, to get a significantly smaller file. Deploying to Bunny.net One great CDN for deploying this is Bunny.net (affiliate link) . They support HTTP Range requests, don’t collect personal data by default, 2 are headquartered in the EU, and offer low-cost access to a global network of CDN and edge storage servers. Pricing varies based on region and replication factor of the edge storage. But generally you pay $0.01/GB ($0.005/GB on the smaller Volume network) for bandwidth to Europe and North America, and $0.01/GB/month (no replication) to $0.055/GB/month (maximum replication) for storage. A high degree of replication mostly matters for latency in case of a cache miss (as the data is further replicated when it’s cached at the CDN PoPs). In practical terms, storing the 139GB world map with replication to most continents (5x) will run you about $5/month in storage fees. Loading a map of Europe on a laptop and zooming in on a city causes about 5MB of data to be transmitted, which would be $0.00005 — further navigations and reloads will be less expensive as more of the map gets cached locally. At $0.05/1k map loads that could be 100x cheaper than Mapbox. However, the actual bandwidth of course varies (less for people that bounce immediately, possibly tens of MB for heavy users). For Mapbox you only pay a flat fee per visit. Uploading the file It’s a good idea to create a storage zone with S3 compatibility enabled, as uploading via the HTTP API timed out after 15 minutes for me. Then, with rclone installed, you can download and stream the file to the Bunny storage zone. Preferably in tmux or from a temporary VPS, if your connection isn’t great. rclone config create bunnycdn s3 \ provider=Other \ access_key_id="<zone-name>" \ secret_access_key="<storage-key>" \ endpoint="https://<primary-region>-s3.storage.bunnycdn.com" rclone copyurl "<build-url>" "bunnycdn:<zone-name>/<filename>.pmtiles" \ --s3-c
articles.summary: Protomaps 推出基于 PMTiles 的自托管地图瓦片方案，单文件即可部署到存储桶，让自建地图服务变得廉价简单。

articles.title: The MacBook Pro's OLED PWM problem
articles.content: Apple has brought tandem OLED technology to the MacBook Pro , joining the Mini-LED display that has served the range since 2021 (and which Apple continues to sell ). Apple calls this a “PROLED XDR Display”. It features individually illuminated pixels, effectively infinite contrast, wonderfully deep blacks and the sort of image quality that Mini-LED, for all its considerable strengths, can’t fully equal. Peak HDR brightness has increased, and Apple has introduced a new display engine designed to manage colour, luminance and pixel usage with extraordinary precision. And of course, in a first for any Apple notebook display, it has touch-input capability. When Apple unveiled the new MacBook Pro, the initial reaction to the screen was overwhelmingly positive. But there’s a burgeoning discussion taking place within the Mac community that deserves attention. On ⁠ MacRumors forums , a thread titled RIP MacBook Pro PROLED for PWM Sensitive Eyes - apple cmon! has attracted people describing remarkably similar experiences. Discussions are also appearing across Reddit, with owners describing discomfort shortly after using their new machines . Some report headaches; others describe a strange sensation of eye fatigue, dizziness, nausea, or an inability to concentrate on the screen for extended periods. Some have already returned the device . Mike Wuerthele, of AppleInsider, published an article on 10 November titled ⁠ If you’re getting dizzy using PROLED MacBook Pro, you are not alone , examining these reports. The following caveat probably doesn't need to be made, but I will make it anyway: these are individual experiences, not evidence that the new MacBook Pro is causing problems for everyone. Plenty of owners are likely perfectly content with (and dazzled by) their new displays. But that isn’t really the point. For the people experiencing these symptoms, the fact that somebody else can happily spend several hours staring at the same screen isn’t particularly reassuring, especially given Apple's long-standing commitment to accessibility. A display can be technically spectacular and still be a spectacularly poor display for a subset of people. PWM Much of the discussion centres on Pulse Width Modulation, or PWM. It’s a technique used to control screen brightness by rapidly switching or modulating the light output. On an OLED display, the pixels themselves produce the light, rather than relying on a separate backlight. By varying the way that light output is modulated, the display can control its apparent brightness. At sufficiently high frequencies, this flickering isn’t something most people can consciously detect. But some people are particularly sensitive to this kind of modulation and can experience eye strain, headaches and other forms of discomfort when looking at displays that use it. articles.title: Things That Turbo Pascal Is Smaller Than (2011)
articles.content: Things That Turbo Pascal is Smaller Than Turbo Pascal 3 for MS-DOS was released in September 1986. Being version 3, there were lesser releases prior to it and flashier ones after, but 3 was a solid representation of the Turbo Pascal experience: a full Pascal compiler, including extensions that it made it practical for commercial use, tightly integrated with an editor. And the whole thing was lightning fast, orders of magnitude faster at building projects than Microsoft's compilers. The entire Turbo Pascal 3.02 executable--the compiler and IDE--was 39,731 bytes. How does that stack up in 2011 terms? Here are some things that Turbo Pascal is smaller than, as of October 30, 2011: The minified version of jquery 1.6 (90,518 bytes). The yahoo.com home page (219,583 bytes). The image of the white iPhone 4S at apple.com (190,157 bytes). zlib.h in the Mac OS X Lion SDK (80,504 bytes). The touch command under OS X Lion (44,016 bytes). Various vim quick reference cards as PDFs. ( This one is 47,508 bytes.) The compiled code for the Erlang R14B02 parser ( erl_parse.beam , 286,324 bytes). The Wikipedia page for C++ (214,251 bytes). (If you liked this, you might like A Personal History of Compilation Speed .) permalink October 30, 2011 previously
articles.summary: 一篇回顾文章列举 Turbo Pascal 3 体积之小，对比现代软件膨胀，凸显早期编译器的高效精简。

articles.title: Microsoft 365 outage leads to chlorine gas poisoning of 15 hotel guests
articles.content: Diesem Problem waren wir alle ausgesetzt: Am Freitag gab es eine Störung, die den US-Softwarekonzern Microsoft lahmgelegt hat. Unter anderem das E-Mail-Programm Outlook. Betroffen war auch das Phantasialand. Durch die Störung kamen keine Mails an, wie das Unternehmen dem WDR am Samstag mitteilte. So bekam niemand mit, dass das Wartungssicherheitssystem der Saunalandschaft längst per Mail Alarm geschlagen hat. Denn das automatischen Dosiersystem hatte zu viel Chlor in den Pool gepumpt. Reizungen der Atemwege Dadurch wurden Gäste im Hotel Ling Bao des Phantasialands in Brühl verletzt. Sie haben über gesundheitliche Probleme geklagt, nachdem sie den Pool besucht hatten. Der wurde zeitweise gesperrt, konnte inzwischen aber wieder freigegeben werden, wie die Feuerwehr am Samstag dem WDR mitteilte. Wegen der Beschwerden der Hotel-Besucher wurden Rettungskräfte und die Feuerwehr gerufen. 13 Gäste klagten über Reizungen der Atemwege, letztlich stieg die Zahl der Betroffenen auf insgesamt 15. Zunächst hieß es, dass fünf Gäste ins Krankenhaus gebracht wurden, später wurde die Zahl auf vier korrigiert, eine Person davon blieb wegen einer mittelschweren Verletzung zur Beobachtung im Krankenhaus. Überhöhter Chlorgehalt Im Hotel ergaben Tests der Einsatzkräfte einen Defekt des automatischen Dosiersystems für den Pool. Dies hatte zu einem deutlich überhöhten Chlorgehalt geführt. Das Wasser wurde daher ausgetauscht. Unsere Quellen: Polizei Rhein-Erft-Kreis Feuerwehr Rhein-Erft-Kreis Pressemeldung Feuerwehr Brühl Birgit Reckersdrees, Direktion Marketing und Sales Phantasialand Sendung: WDR2, WDR-Aktuell, 14.11.2026, 18 Uhr Sendung: WDR Fernsehen, WDR aktuell, 15.11.2026, 12.45 Uhr
articles.summary: 微软 365 服务中断导致酒店邮件系统失效，间接造成 15 名客人氯气中毒，暴露关键系统对云服务依赖的风险。

articles.title: A datetime library for Rust
articles.content: Jiff is a datetime library for Rust that encourages you to jump into the pit of success . Jiff automatically handles many common problems related to daylight saving time by putting time zone handling front and center into the API. Jiff has already seen widespread adoption in the Rust ecosystem. Jiff is pronounced like “gif” with a soft “g,” as in “gem.” This blog announces the Jiff 1.0 release by giving a tour of its API. Target audience : Rust programmers who need convenient datetime handling. Table of Contents The Jiff 1.0 Commitment Introduction Follow Along Terms The DateTime Onion Defining a time zone Durations When should I use Jiff? Parsing and Formatting FromStr and Display The “friendly” Duration Format strptime and strftime The jiff::fmt module Locale Sensitive Formatting via ICU4X Integration Date Manipulation Date Basics Date Arithmetic Date Rounding Other Calendars Which DateTime Type Do I Use? Span Manipulation Conclusion Motivation Inspiration The Jiff 1.0 Commitment Jiff is already used in production in many projects: uv, Cargo, Starship, fd, Nushell, mise, Jujutsu, uutils/coreutils and even as the basis for a Temporal implementation in AWS LLRT. It is time to call it 1.0. Unless some significant defect is found in Jiff’s API, my plan is to commit to Jiff 1.0 indefinitely. This is important because the intent is for Jiff to be an ecosystem building block that appears in the public API of other libraries. This makes Jiff an attractive public dependency, which means semver incompatible releases are likely to cause significant pain in the ecosystem. They will not be made lightly. To see a list of breaking changes between Jiff 0.2 and Jiff 1.0, please consult the CHANGELOG . Introduction In programming, a datetime library’s core functionality rests at the intersection of a computer system’s concept of time and a human’s concept of time. The prevailing notion of system time is Unix time . A human’s concept of time is far more complex, but the most popular such model is the Gregorian calendar coupled with either a 12-hour or 24-hour clock. At the core of every datetime library rests some routine for converting between these concepts. A datetime library typically provides much more than this. Indeed, datetime handling has historically been very difficult . My own belief is that the difficulty comes from poor modeling of the domain . Instead of encapsulating the complexity inside a reusable bundle of code, many datetime libraries pass some or all of the complexity on to its users. Jiff instead tries hard to encapsulate the complexity and make it difficult for users to do something wrong. ( Jiff is not the first to do this! ) In this section of the blog, we’ll do some very basic introductions. articles.title: All AI-generated code should be Open Source
articles.content: All AI-generated code should be Open Source This may be a hot take, but I strongly believe that all code generated by AI should be Open Source. And here's why. First of all, AI models were trained on a massive corpus of Open Source code written since RMS announced the GNU Project and the Free Software Movement. That code was simply scraped from the internet and used without permission or proper attribution. The models were also trained on Stack Overflow and Stack Exchange sister projects, which are released under Creative Commons licenses that legally require attribution. Turning this collective knowledge into proprietary, closed-source code feels like license laundering. The second reason is legal: purely AI -generated code is not written by a human, meaning it should not be copyrightable. The foundation for this principle in the US goes back to the famous Monkey Selfie dispute , which established that non-humans cannot hold copyrights. A precedent later cited by the U.S. Copyright Office regarding AI . Following the same logic, Wikimedia Commons requires all purely AI -generated images to be tagged as Public Domain . However, copyright laws differ across the globe. For instance, countries like the UK grant limited copyright protection to computer-generated works. To make things fair across all jurisdictions, and to honor the open ecosystem that made AI possible, developers and companies should explicitly release AI -generated code under Open Source licenses or dedicate it to the public domain using the Creative Commons Zero (CC0) license. Of course, code is not always 100% manual or 100% automated. However, developers more and more rely on AI without even reviewing the generated output, let alone modifying it to fit their specific needs. Code like this, where humans put little effort, except writing prompts, should definitely be Open Source. If you find this article interesting you may want to follow me on Twitter: @jcubic and on LinkedIn . See hacker news for discussion

articles.title: 25 of my favourite modern NES games
articles.content: We are in the middle of the Second ReNESance (the first one is the one that saved the video game industry in North America). The combined decades of research and knowledge on how the venerable little NES works have produced a true cornucopia of games. We are all lucky to be here to witness it. I am always happy to inform video game fans that the Nintendo Entertainment System is still receiving lots and lots of new third-party games. In alphabetical order, because I refuse to rank them, here are 25 of my favourite modern NES games. Almost all can be obtained digitally, usually from the developer or publisher, most for a modest fee. Digital NES downloads are cheap! Most of these can also be obtained as physical cartridges for the true hi-fi experience on original hardware. All Hell Unleashed (back to top) A little spooky, very pixelly. This game is a real gem. Made by 8-bit Slasher who has been honing his skills in other horror games for the NES, All Hell Unleashed is an extensive love letter to the horror slashers of the 1980s and 1990s. There is an underlying story about an evil cult that is trying to resurrect something or other, but that’s just an excuse plot so that you can fight Jaws, Freddy, Jason, Ghostface and others. It works surprisingly well. You can select your favourite horror movie from a stage-select screen to do your platforming as you fight the forces of evil, culminating in the boss fights where the villain of each horror franchise swoops in for a mano-a-mano . The platforming feels good, and the boss fights function as set pieces showcasing the real villains we are here to see in their 8-bit glory. Finally Jason dons a better outfit on the NES than that silly purple jumpsuit! After each classic horror villain is defeated, it is time to take on the cult itself for one final showdown. Definitely a spine-tingling adventure! Alwa’s Awakening (back to top) Alwa’s Awakening was originally a PC game made with pseudo-NES limitations (and in the case of the music, with actual NES limitations, as the developer used Famitracker to compose all of the music). If it doesn’t feel like a classic NES game and instead plays more like a modern indie Metroidvania, that’s because it is. In the game, you play as Zoe, a girl who likes video games and one day awakens in the mystical land of Alwa, a place from one of her games. Your task is to guide Zoe through an adventure in Alwa where she will uncover power-ups that open up new avenues of adventure. Typical Metroidvania stuff, although a bit shorter than most games in the genre. The PC-to-NES port of this game was handled by my good friend Brad Smith of Lizard fame. He made a couple of interesting YouTube videos describing the process. VIDEO VIDEO The game looks absolutely gorgeous for the NES, and its Famitracker-composed soundtrack made it through the porting process completely unscathed. There was a limited physical edition that today is only available via secondhand markets. If you can grab a cop

articles.title: Let Me Let You Own Your Data
articles.content: Why do I have to choose between my web app respecting people’s privacy and it, like… having basic functionality? When I was working on Cheapskate , I realized after a few weeks that there was a fundamental issue. The app relies on Supabase for the unsexy parts of its architecture: authentication and a SQL datastore. All of it is bog-standard and all of it I happily handed off to be someone else’s problem. To be clear, I love Supabase – if I had to run all that boilerplate myself, I never would have made Cheapskate. But… the shape of it is wrong. I don’t want to own this data. This is a person’s financial details! Shouldn’t that live with them, and not with me? Is it even possible to make a web app like this, with anything close to the same convenience and functionality (durable, works across devices, shareable with friends) as Supabase allows? Well, I really wanted to. I spent a lot of time trying. Here are all the things that don’t work: localStorage : the easiest one to try, and doesn’t require user accounts, but the inability to access data across devices or share with someone else makes it a non-starter showDirectoryPicker : cool, and durable (unlike localStorage), but not yet supported by all browsers, and sharing (while possible) requires an extra service, e.g. Dropbox or iCloud CloudKit Private Database : Apple’s obscure BaaS! Locks us into Apple SSO, requires a $99 Apple Developer subscription, and the JS library doesn’t implement sharing anyway SQLite in Google Drive : cute, but it similarly locks us into Google SSO, and I actually tried this, it was miserable to set up both as a user and a developer B-Y-O-DynamoDB : this is actually how I made Cardi a few years ago! It works great… other than how it is insane to ask people to “log in” using AWS keys lol remoteStorage : really cool, and the Platonic ideal of this concept, but support is thin, and the docs explicitly call out collaboration as unsupported CRDT / “local-first” : again cool, but I haven’t seen a mature “Firebase for CRDTs” like the one proposed, and it’s unclear if it would even solve the privacy aspect Besides, all of these options compromise on the data model anyway, being KV or blob storage when all I really want is an API to run SQL queries. You know, like any normal app? Argh!

articles.title: cursor:pointer on buttons
articles.content: Cursors Cursors Cursors Cursors Published on: November 13, 2026 Categories: CSSWG 8 , CSS 96 , Opinion Current music: Envy — Connected Voice Current drink: Peppermint Tea Three weeks ago, at a CSS Working Grouping meeting, we discussed an issue “ Cursors for base appearance ” , and resolved on the following: The CSS Working Group just discussed [css-forms-1] Cursors for base appearance, and agreed to the following: RESOLVED: Adopt cursor rules in the last comment. SUMMARY: Pointer = “click this thing”, text cursor says “prepare to enter text”, grabbing hand says “drag this”. One of the rules from the “last comment” mentioned there is select , option , input [ type = checkbox ], input [ type = radio ], button , input [ type = button ], input [ type = submit ], input [ type = reset ], input [ type = color ], input [ type = image ], :: file-selector-button { cursor : pointer; } Or, if we were to remove all non-button selectors, button { cursor : pointer; } That is, of course, not a change to the default styles in the browser — this is a rule for elements that will have an appearance: base-… . Also note that, this user agent style will be very much overrideable — no !important . Anyone who does not like cursor: pointer on buttons and other similar elements, are free to override it to default (or anything else) in their stylesheets. The rest of us can, I guess, celebrate? I was always on the side of this decision. I published my “ Correct Cursor on Active Elements ” article in 2013. In 2017, I opened my first CSSWG issue — “ Change the pointer cursor to indicate any interactive element ” , which led to a change in a non-normative part of the spec. Since then, I did not see any new arguments in this debate. I will not repeat everything that I argued about, but one of the most common counter-arguments that I read today is “OS does not do it”. Did you see that “OS”? When was the last time your OS innovated anything in the UI? Did it become easier to use over years? Many of people with this argument ask, thinking that this will be a good question, something like “What next — change the cursor in the OS?!”. I mean… Yes? I would be happy with that. When I look at like half of the (non-native) apps in my desktop OS, they have cursor: pointer on interactive elements. Cinny, Discord, Signal, Slack, Steam, VS Code — some of the apps that I have before me. When I use apps that do not change the cursor to anything other than default , I cringe. Default cursor does not communicate anything. It does one job well — point at a specific pixel. It could do more. In the issue, many people came with dislikes and their arguments against cursor: pointer . I want to aknowledge one argument that I fully agree with — it would be great if buttons and links would have different cursors. And also, regular links should have cursors different from the links that are opened in new tabs. We need more cursors. But if we were to look at those three things: Blank space on the page. But

articles.title: FreeBSD bhyve Live Migration: Moving VMs Between Hosts
articles.content: This project presents a first working state for live migration of bhyve guests on FreeBSD 15.1. A running amd64 guest can move between two hosts over TCP while continuing to run; it is paused only for the final stop-and-copy phase. The work builds on bhyve's experimental snapshot support and adds dirty-page tracking in the vmm kernel module together with a migration protocol in bhyve and bhyvectl. Live migration of a VM in FreeBSD with bhyve I previously discussed the state of bhyve live migration, its historical development, existing limitations, and why it matters for the future of FreeBSD virtualization in my article bhyve on FreeBSD and VM Live Migration – Quo vadis? . The goal is deliberately practical: make it possible to test, discuss, and improve a real implementation rather than discuss live migration only in the abstract. The current code and test tooling are being published as a WIP RFC so that the next steps can be shaped in the open. A more detailed demonstration of a VM being live migrated can be watched on my YouTube channel . Why this matters Live migration is an important building block for enterprise virtualisation. It enables host maintenance, hardware replacement, load balancing, and failure-domain management with far less disruption to workloads. It is also central to the Sylve project, which aims to offer a Proxmox-like virtualisation solution for FreeBSD. Migration is not an optional convenience in that kind of platform; it is one of the capabilities that makes clustered operations practical. It is equally important for BoxyBSD, where I offer free BSD-based VPS instances to individuals. Without a credible migration path, routine host work can require a guest outage. That makes live migration a current show stopper for the project, and is why this work is being pushed toward a testable, reviewable state. How the current implementation works The source starts with a pre-copy phase. It sends populated guest memory, then repeatedly obtains a bitmap of pages changed since the previous scan and sends only those pages. Once the remaining dirty set fits the configured downtime target, stops shrinking, or reaches the configured round limit, bhyve pauses the guest and its devices. It then sends the final dirty pages and the existing snapshot state for the vCPUs, kernel state, and emulated devices. The destination validates the basic VM geometry, receives memory and state, restores it, and reports that it is ready. Only then does the source send GO , the commit point. Before GO , a failed migration can resume the source guest. The destination does not start the guest if it does not receive that commit message. A warm, stop-and-copy mode is available too, which is useful both as a fallback and as a comparison baseline. What is implemented today Pre-copy and warm migration: live pre-copy is configurable with downtime and maximum-round controls; explicit stop-and-copy migration is also supported. articles.title: A NES emulator written in Odin
articles.content: A NES emulator written in Odin I made a NES emulator in Odin ! Github link Intro I’ve started this project in late June of 2024. I’ve worked on it in my spare time off and on. I decided to put a pause on this project in January 2025 to focus on other things. I’ve learned so much about: The NES architecture, and possibly about game console architectures in general Bits and bytes, hex notation, and bitwise operations. The Odin programming language. I haven’t used it on a serious project before. How computers work. CPU instructions, “cycles”, etc Emulation. It’s very hard. Respect to emulator developers! It’s been a wild ride. I’ve had a lot of fun, but I’ve also suffered more towards the end, when trying to make the emulator “fully” accurate. You can read the Github Readme for more info about the project. Features Enough emulation accuracy to run Battletoads and hundreds of other games perfectly. Debugger view with some debugging features Menu view to interact with the emulator Save states Controller support CRT Shader toggle (Partial) Sound Supported Mappers: NROM, MMC1, UXROM, CNROM, MMC3, GxROM, AxROM Making an emulator I’ve seen some people say that making a NES emulator is a simple weekend project, and I frankly found that baffling. Because evidently , it’s not. It took me 7 months to get my emulator to how it is now. I think what they actually mean is that getting a NES emulator “working” takes a short time. Like maybe getting Donkey Kong to run. And that’s true. You can get to 80% or maybe 90% pretty fast. It’s the last 10% that takes a long, long time. The NES hardware has many idiosyncrasies that need to be emulated for certain games to run. Many games depend on very specific NES behavior. And if you don’t implement it right, they won’t run. A lot of the challenge is about timing. The CPU and the PPU (the chip that handles the graphics rendering in the NES) run in parallel and they communicate with each other. That timing needs to be very accurate, or many wrong things can happen. Most games will run fine with a less than accurate emulator, but a lot of them won’t, and they will need you to consider things in more detail. Another issue is mappers . Mappers are what we call an implementation of a type of cartridge. You see, NES games come in cartridges, and cartridges aren’t just data. They are circuitry with their own behavior and extra resources like read-only memory, and writable memory. Some come with extra audio capabilities, but I haven’t implemented that. Anyway, you have to implement these mappers if you want a game that comes in that cartridge to run in your game. They complete the NES’s circuitry. In a way, they are a part of the NES hardware. There are many mappers, but you can support a lot of games by just implementing a few. I’ve had trouble implementing some mappers, and some of them are still badly implemented, causing some games to not work. I found it hard to understand some of the mapper documentation. articles.title: Please Implement A Quorum Database
articles.content: Please Implement A Quorum Database Posted 2026-11-15 18 minute reading time Mandatory Legal Disclaimer: Opinions expressed are solely my own and do not express the views or opinions of my employer. I return with part two of the replication rants series. This talk was given at HPTS'26 and fleshes out the argument for quorum-based replication in Enough With All The Raft , and continues to build off of the work that went into writing Data Replication Design Spectrum . I think we tend to view quorum replication as generally impractical for production use. I think that is an outdated view. Video VIDEO If you want the links to papers, find the corresponding slide below. Transcript This is a replication talk that I gave at HPTS 2026. I once did a survey of what type of replication algorithm databases in production are using, and the result looks like this. Raft is the giant pacman, eating the primary-backup and quorum slices. The Quorum slice is small enough that we can just fully enumerate it right now. Upper left are OSS majority quorum databases. Upper right are proprietary ones that used or are using it for data replication. Bottom left are proprietary ones using consensus for a log. Bottom right are technically true but carry caveats. If we filter that list by how they’re doing now: Riak is long past hedge fund dead. Voldemort is so dead all that all of you forgot it existed until the previous slide. InfluxDB and Grafana Mimir had previous iterations which used quorums, and then they re-architected. Weviate does quorum for data and raft for metadata, and I won’t be shocked if they re-architected too. Google Megastore is basically dead. Tencent PaxosStore is super internal in chinese bigtech, so I have no idea. CouchDB was more meant for eventual consistency but has a clustered mode, and I have no idea who uses it other than cloudant? OG Dynamo, which someone here can tell me about, but I’m assuming is/has been phased out? Note: the HPTS audience head shaking agreed with my assessment of Dynamo. Which leaves me with this awkward feeling that if I say implement a quorum database, the only good example I have to point to is Cassandra?!? HPTS says submit your spicy takes, so brace yourself: I think we should be credibly building more than one good example of a quorum database. Which we are! I’m holding out 3 very recent examples on you. But first, for the next 16 minutes I will be CEO and utterly delusional founder of CashDB, because I need a running example for this talk. CashDB is a database specialized for whatever your splitting-the-bill-with-friends app that you use. It has two major limitations. articles.content: Chrome DevTools for agents Chrome DevTools for agents ( chrome-devtools-mcp ) lets your coding agent (such as Antigravity, Claude, Cursor or Copilot) control and inspect a live Chrome browser. It is available as a Model-Context-Protocol (MCP) server and as a CLI . Both give your AI coding assistant access to the full power of Chrome DevTools for reliable automation, in-depth debugging, and performance analysis. Tool reference | CLI | Skills | Changelog | Contributing | Troubleshooting | Design Principles Get performance insights : Uses Chrome DevTools to record traces and extract actionable performance insights. Advanced browser debugging : Analyze network requests, take screenshots and check browser console messages (with source-mapped stack traces). Reliable automation . Uses puppeteer to automate actions in Chrome and automatically wait for action results. chrome-devtools-mcp exposes content of the browser instance to the MCP clients allowing them to inspect, debug, and modify any data in the browser or DevTools. Avoid sharing sensitive or personal information that you don't want to share with MCP clients. chrome-devtools-mcp officially supports Google Chrome and Chrome for Testing only. Other Chromium-based browsers may work, but this is not guaranteed, and you may encounter unexpected behavior. Use at your own discretion. We are committed to providing fixes and support for the latest version of Extended Stable Chrome . Performance tools may send trace URLs to the Google CrUX API to fetch real-user experience data. This helps provide a holistic performance picture by presenting field data alongside lab data. This data is collected by the Chrome User Experience Report (CrUX) . To disable this, run with the --no-performance-crux flag. Google collects usage statistics (such as tool invocation success rates, latency, and environment information) to improve the reliability and performance of Chrome DevTools MCP. Data collection is enabled by default . You can opt-out by passing the --no-usage-statistics flag when starting the server: "args" : [ " -y " , " chrome-devtools-mcp@latest " , " --no-usage-statistics " ] Google handles this data in accordance with the Google Privacy Policy . Google's collection of usage statistics for Chrome DevTools MCP is independent from the Chrome browser's usage statistics. Opting out of Chrome metrics does not automatically opt you out of this tool, and vice-versa. Collection is disabled if CHROME_DEVTOOLS_MCP_NO_USAGE_STATISTICS or CI env variables are set. By default, the server periodically checks the npm registry for updates and logs a notification when a newer version is available. You can disable these update checks by setting the CHROME_DEVTOOLS_MCP_NO_UPDATE_CHECKS environment variable. articles.title: Tesla opens Cybercab pre-orders ‘for personal use,’ with geo restrictions and a $299 monthly fee
articles.content: Tesla said on Friday evening that “select customers” now have the opportunity to pre-order the company’s autonomous, golden Cybercab “for personal use.” More details became clear as those select customers looked at the order page. Tech reviewer Marques Brownlee posted that buyers “must accept delivery” in one of a handful of Texas cities and that the Cybercab will only operate in certain geofenced areas. The estimated delivery date is December 2026. In addition to the $29,990 price tag, Cybercab owners will need to pay $299 per month to operate their vehicle. In response to Brownlee’s post, Tesla CEO Elon Musk said the Cybercab “will be available nationwide, as we receive regulatory approval.” He added that the monthly fee is “too high”: “Should match the cost of Tesla [Full Self-Driving] and connectivity for other models, which is more like ~$115/month.” Tesla’s Ashok Elluswamy offered more information about the geofencing, saying that Cybercab will work “unsupervised inside all the same geo locations as @robotaxi, just serving the owners’ needs.” After falling far short of projected sales, Tesla recently announced it will cease Cybertruck production next year and use the additional factory capacity to build more Cybercabs.
articles.summary: 特斯拉开放Cybercab个人用途预订，设地理限制并收取每月299美元费用，交付细节随之曝光。

articles.title: SpaceX returned its Starship rocket on Saturday—but there's a catch
articles.content: STARBASE, Texas —The black and silver ship fell out of the sky, emerging from the cloud deck near the very end of its flight. Incongruously, the rocket flew horizontal until the last moment when three Raptor rocket engines ignited and it swooped into a vertical position. Slowly, gently, haltingly, the Starship upper stage eased its way toward the waiting tower where two arms extended outward, awaiting expectantly. The margins are so incredibly narrow. Two nubs on either side of the rocket, each protruding only about one foot, were the only purchase the rocket would have on the arms. Then, less than a minute after it came into view, the Starship upper stage was snagged by the launch tower, as snug as you like. And so it was all over. SpaceX, nearly a quarter of a century after its founding, had just taken a hugely significant step toward developing and optimizing a massive, rapidly reusable rocket. We are dazzled This was a breathtaking feat; a brilliant technical achievement that required the best engineering minds to think through a million different, difficult problems. And on Saturday evening, following a handful of practice runs into the Indian Ocean, they did it before the entire world. Watching Starship launch from here a little less than a day earlier, and knowing it had orbited the planet multiple times, added to the sense of unreality in seeing this spaceship return to Earth under its own power, and be captured by the tower. It felt like stepping into the future. SpaceX has dazzled us before, by landing rockets on barges and returning humans to space with Crew Dragon. But this flight took things to another level. Starships are huge. They carry a huge amount of energy coming back from orbit. And until a few years ago, it seemed beyond fantastical to think about capturing a rocket with what are essentially outsized chopsticks. Nevertheless, it happened. Rapid reuse is firmly on the horizon Humans have built reusable spacecraft that flew into orbit before. In the 1970s, flush with confidence after the triumphant Moon landings, NASA designed and built several Space Shuttles. They had solid rocket boosters that were fished from the ocean and reused. The large orange external tank was not recovered after each flight, but the orbiters went to space for two weeks, or even longer, before returning to Earth and landing on a runway. The shuttles were engineering marvels. But during the return to Earth they acted as gliders, not igniting their engines. And their heat shields were delicate flowers, requiring painstaking refurbishment after each flight. At the outset of the shuttle program, the space agency contemplated sending dozens of humans into space at a time, and carrying cargo at a cost as low of $25 per pound. Reality never matched these rosy projections. The crew space capped out at seven astronauts, and the cost-per-pound was closer to $25,000. articles.summary: Google开源AQuA参考实现，用于分析生产环境AI代理会话、验证失败模式并定位根因，实测显著减少错误。

articles.content: Netflix is developing an ontology-driven knowledge graph to accelerate production investigations and provide AI agents with a shared understanding of its operational environment. By Craig Risi
articles.summary: Netflix构建本体驱动的知识图谱，将运营数据转化为AI可理解的共享语义，加速生产故障排查与可观测性。

articles.title: AI Weekly Issue #543: Google is the latest tech giant to chase TypeSafe's 8-week-old Jev
articles.content: This issue is about decision models, a new kind of AI model that does not write text. You give it an input and a fixed list of answers, and it returns the best answer with a probability, in milliseconds. TypeSafe AI released the first one, Jev, on September 15. On Wednesday Google released its own, after OpenAI and Microsoft did in October, and all three charge $0.10 or less per million input tokens and nothing for output. Shanghai AI Lab says its 4B model beat Jev on its tests, and Microsoft built its model on Alibaba's Qwen. Chatbots still score a little higher on the hardest decisions, at 15 times the cost. In the middle: on Vercel's gateway, decision models took one in four AI requests in October.
articles.summary: TypeSafe AI于9月发布决策模型Jev，输入问题与固定答案列表即可毫秒级返回最佳答案，Google随后推出竞品。

articles.title: AI Weekly Issue #542: AI week ahead: data center pause backers could win 15 governor races
articles.content: This issue is about the week ahead, and something is scheduled almost every day. On Tuesday, US voters choose 36 governors, and in up to 15 of those races the candidate who backs a pause on new data centers could win. Apple reports earnings today and AMD on Tuesday. On Wednesday, Apple starts testing Apple Intelligence in China with Alibaba's Qwen, and Agility Robotics expects to close its deal to go public. When Congress returns on November 9, OpenAI plans to push for "speed limits" on the most powerful AI. Last week, a fake Claude Code update reached up to 5,000 Cursor users, and in a Cornell and Yale test nine of ten AI models raised their own spending limits. In the middle: insuring Big Tech's debt now costs more than at any time since 2021.
articles.summary: AI Weekly前瞻：美国36州州长选举中，最多15个州支持暂停新建数据中心的候选人可能胜出；苹果、AMD本周发布财报。

articles.title: AI Weekly Issue #541: Big Tech reports AI spending Wednesday as CoreWeave debt hits distress
articles.content: This issue looks ahead. On Wednesday the Fed announces its rate decision, then Microsoft and Alphabet report after the close. Amazon follows on Thursday. Investors want to know whether AI spending is still paying off, and the credit market is already nervous: insurance against a CoreWeave default now costs more than 10% a year. Anthropic is expected to file its IPO paperwork publicly any day. Moonshot says Kimi K3.1 Pro's open weights arrive November 4. Israel votes on Tuesday after a campaign full of AI deepfakes, and the US midterms are a week from Tuesday. In the middle: so far, AI has paid off for the companies that sell it, not the ones that buy it.
articles.summary: 微软、Alphabet周三发布财报，投资者关注AI支出回报；CoreWeave债务违约保险成本飙升，信贷市场对AI泡沫显现担忧。

articles.title: AI Weekly Issue #540: AI is finding software flaws faster than teams can fix them
articles.content: This Applied AI edition looks at what organizations actually did with AI over the past two weeks, drawn from our Use-Case Library and from SEC filings. Three things stand out: AI now finds security flaws at record volume, AI agents do a large share of the work at some companies, and test agents keep doing things nobody asked them to do.
articles.summary: Applied AI报告显示，AI发现安全漏洞的速度已超过团队修复能力，部分公司AI代理承担大量工作，测试代理持续扩张。

articles.title: AI Weekly Issue #539: AI-made midterm ads top $137 million, and 70% carry no AI label
articles.content: Campaigns and PACs have spent more than $137 million on AI-generated or AI-enhanced midterm ads, and about 70% of them carry no AI label, the New York Times reported. The biggest pro-AI super PAC network paid about $20 million to a Nevada company that exists only as a post office box. A new report found 81 of 134 AI models failed a test built from terrorist-style questions. A video game reverse engineering site is closing because AI made the work too easy. Some companies that rushed into AI are now limiting it, and a JAMA study counted 270 million questions doctors asked one AI tool. In the middle: police in Michigan used an AI-generated photo of a teenager to catch a suspect.
articles.summary: 中期选举中AI生成或增强的广告支出超1.37亿美元，约70%未标注AI标签，最大亲AI超级PAC向空壳公司支付约2000万美元。

articles.title: AI Weekly Issue #537: AI models may soon copy themselves onto smart fridges, Anthropic says
articles.content: This issue is built from the links the AI experts we follow shared most since our last issue on October 8, minus the stories we already sent you in the Daily Espresso. The most shared: Anthropic's warning that small AI models may soon be able to copy themselves onto home devices. Also: a large study of what AI coding agents change at real companies, a fight over how to check AI math proofs, creative workers pushing back on AI, and police buying more AI.
articles.summary: Anthropic警告小型AI模型可能很快能自我复制到智能冰箱等家用设备，成为本周AI专家分享最多的消息。

articles.title: AI Weekly Issue #536: Top AI models failed a test of inventing new AI research
articles.content: This issue is built from the links the AI experts we follow shared over the past three days. Most of them look ahead: whether AI can do AI research on its own, who gets a say in governing it, how it is moving into war planning, and how it is moving onto personal computers.
articles.summary: 顶尖AI模型未能通过自主开展AI研究的测试，专家同时关注AI治理话语权、军事规划应用及进入个人电脑的趋势。

articles.title: AI Weekly Issue #535: AI got too expensive, so companies are moving to cheaper models
articles.content: This Applied AI edition looks at what organizations actually did with AI over the past three weeks. Three patterns stand out: companies switching models to control cost, large deployments that are now in daily use, and a growing list of places where AI was restricted or removed.
articles.summary: AI成本过高促使企业转向更便宜的模型，大型部署已进入日常使用，同时越来越多场景对AI实施限制或移除。

articles.title: AI Weekly Issue #534: Universities cannot grade their way out of AI
articles.content: This week, campus IT leaders voted AI their top priority for the first time, Cambridge refused Turnitin's new terms over AI training on student work, Dartmouth opened an investigation into its own provost's writing, and Ken Griffin gave Carnegie Mellon $3 billion. Student AI use is no longer a future scenario. The useful question for universities is whether they can teach students to work with AI and still certify what those students can do without it. New evidence from tutoring trials, assessment redesigns, student-support systems and campus data deals points to a practical answer.
articles.summary: 高校IT负责人首次将AI列为首要任务；剑桥拒绝Turnitin AI训练条款，达特茅斯调查教务长写作，AI使用已非未来议题。

articles.title: AI Weekly Issue #533: Meta tested human callers behind its AI phone agent
articles.content: The AI story of September 22–28 was not simply that agents became more capable. It was that their hidden handoffs became visible: a supposedly automated call could reach a contractor, a supposedly private prompt or image could reach a reviewer, a monitor could detect an agent long before a person stopped it, and a local app flaw could inherit every permission a user had granted. The new AI Weekly Who’s Who census points to one practical question: when an agent crosses a boundary, who knows—and who can still intervene?
articles.summary: Meta的AI电话代理被曝背后有真人承包商接手，暴露自动化系统的隐藏人工交接，以及提示词和图像流向审核人员的问题。

articles.title: All your packages are belong to us
articles.content: AI agents can write the code, choose the packages, and run the install. Who's checking what they just invited onto your machine? This week I'm joined by Ahmad Nassri, CTO of Socket and former CTO of npm. We get into the trust built into a package install, the new ways attackers are using agents, and what it takes to keep building without handing over the keys or your wallet.
articles.summary: Socket CTO Ahmad Nassri 做客播客，讨论 AI 代理自动选包安装带来的供应链信任风险，以及攻击者利用代理的新手法。

articles.title: We now have Kerr’s Law
articles.content: Dave Kerr created hacker laws, and now he finds himself reviewing agent-written code for them. Back on the show after six years, Dave names what he sees limiting teams today: keeping everyone’s mental model in sync with what’s actually been built. Adam declares it Kerr’s Law on the spot. We get into why Dave’s team treats code review as a deliberate slowdown, how Shellwright lets agents bring evidence to a pull request, and what living with bipolar disorder has taught Dave about noticing when the excitement of these tools stops being healthy.
articles.summary: Dave Kerr 提出“Kerr 定律”，指出团队最大瓶颈是成员心智模型与实际构建产物脱节，尤其在审查 AI 生成代码时。

articles.title: The future is Postgres
articles.content: Craig Kerstiens returns to talk about the ever-expanding world of Postgres: a deliberately boring core, a thriving extension ecosystem, and pg_lake bringing DuckDB and Iceberg into the mix. We dig into the pain of ETL, what Craig is watching in Postgres 19, the impact of AI on open source maintainers, and why the database still has plenty of room to grow.
articles.summary: Craig Kerstiens 谈 Postgres 生态扩张：核心保持简单、扩展繁荣，pg_lake 引入 DuckDB 与 Iceberg，并讨论 AI 对维护者的影响。

articles.title: Building what's next
articles.content: This week I'm talking with Zeno Rocha, CEO of Resend, about scaling "boring" email to 3 million users, the secret Go rewrite behind it, and building for agents. We cover pricing.md, MCP, spam gangs, and why Resend keeps what's next for email.
articles.summary: Resend CEO Zeno Rocha 分享如何用 Go 重写支撑 300 万用户的邮件服务，并介绍面向 AI 代理的 pricing.md 与 MCP 实践。

articles.title: From zero to NanoClaw
articles.content: Gavriel Cohen, creator of NanoClaw and co-founder of NanoCo, joins Adam to explain how a 40-hour weekend project became a viral open source hit and the foundation of an enterprise AI company. Gavriel describes the security concerns that led him to build a small, container-isolated alternative to OpenClaw, why he released it under the MIT license, and why the project's community and credibility are more valuable than keeping its code private. They explore the shift from writing code to architecting the environments in which agents work, NanoClaw's "skills over features" approach, the approval and governance layers required inside large companies, and a future where every worker manages agents without surrendering human judgment. They close with the technical simplicity behind NanoClaw, containers, TypeScript, SQLite, and a two-database design, and Adam's case for durable Agent Flow artifacts that keep organizational context from disappearing into chat.
articles.summary: Gavriel Cohen 讲述周末 40 小时做出的 NanoClaw 如何爆红开源，并因安全顾虑打造容器隔离方案，进而创办企业 AI 公司 NanoCo。

articles.title: Changelog IRL @ PlanetScale (Sept 17, 2026)
articles.content: Changelog is taking over PlanetScale's HQ We’re getting together IRL!! On Thursday, September 17th, Changelog is taking over PlanetScale’s HQ in San Francisco for an evening of short talks and conversations about AI, developer tools and what people are building. We’ll have a few conversations with special guests and time for questions, food, drinks and hanging out. I’ll be joined by three builders pushing this idea forward, starting with Dan Robinson from Detail (detail.dev), with more guests to be announced very soon. I also have 80 limited edition t-shirts printed to give away! This won’t be a few presentations followed by everyone heading home. We’re doing this Changelog-style: live conversations, questions from the room, drinks, and plenty of time afterward for the hallway track. If you’re in San Francisco, register to come hang out! Changelog IRL Thursday, September 17th, 2026 6:00pm – 9:00pm PDT PlanetScale HQ 108 Natoma St, San Francisco, CA 94105 Speakers Dan Robinson, (Detail) Christian Glassiognon, Developer Educator at PlanetScale TBD Schedule 6:00 - 6:45pm: Doors open, food, drinks and networking 6:45 - 7:00pm: Welcome and opening chat with Adam 7:00 - 8:00pm: Changelog IRL with Dan and special guests 8:00 - 8:15pm: Questions 8:30 - 9:00pm: Hanging out and networking 9:00pm: Close All times Pacific. PlanetScale HQ, 108 Natoma St, San Francisco.
articles.summary: Changelog 将于 2026 年 9 月 17 日在旧金山 PlanetScale 总部举办线下活动，围绕 AI 与开发者工具展开短演讲与交流。

articles.title: Forking Cal.com to closed source
articles.content: This week I'm joined by Peer Richelsen, co-founder of Cal.com. What if the majority of open source repositories are already compromised and we just don't know it yet? That's the theory Peer brings to the table this week. We dig into how AI has flattened the knowledge graph to the point that a 16-year-old can vibe hack a power station just as easily as their mom can vibe code an iOS app, why the reporting culture that has kept open source safe all these years is collapsing under AI generated noise, Cal.com's move to fork its own codebase and take the sensitive parts private, and the eye opening reality that shipping "$1 of AI tokens for pennies on the dollar" is now a common startup business model.
articles.summary: Cal.com 联合创始人 Peer Richelsen 提出多数开源仓库可能已被攻陷，并讨论 AI 降低知识门槛后开源与闭源的分叉选择。

articles.title: Postgres at PlanetScale
articles.content: Sam Lambert is back after 4 years and he does not hold back! We cover $5 PlanetScale Postgres, the Neki "do-over" of Vitess, agents shipping schema changes through deploy requests, rolling back a 500TB table in seconds, and the very real question of whether to open source any of it. Plus: why he thinks the sleeping, lazy giants should be broken up.
articles.summary: PlanetScale CEO Sam Lambert 介绍 5 美元 Postgres、Vitess 重写、代理提交 schema 变更及秒级回滚 500TB 表等新进展。

articles.title: Canary tokens and digital tripwires
articles.content: Haroon Meer is back! Haroon is the Founder of Thinkst, the ~50-person bootstrapped company behind Canary and Canarytokens — honeypots and tripwires you sprinkle inside your network and forget about until an attacker touches one. We talk about the AWS API key token attackers just can't resist trying, the real credit card token backed by an actual bank partnership, Breadcrumbs (their brand-new feature that leads intruders straight to your canaries), a live demo where a hardware Canary becomes a Synology NAS in one click, and how a company with zero outbound sales and no price increase in ten years quietly passed $22.5 million in ARR.
articles.summary: Thinkst 创始人 Haroon Meer 介绍 Canary 蜜罐与数字绊线，讲述攻击者屡试不爽的 AWS API Key 诱饵等实战经验。

articles.title: From open source hits to OpenAI
articles.content: This week I'm talking with Max Stoiber, currently working on ChatGPT's plugin directory and app platform at OpenAI. We discuss the hundreds of open source projects nobody remembers alongside the big ones like react-boilerplate and styled-components, how Spectrum became part of GitHub and eventually helped shape GitHub Discussions, the founder growth that came from building Stellate, the GraphQL cache that turned into a dual acquisition by Shopify and The Guild, and why ChatGPT apps feel like a new surface for software.
articles.summary: Max Stoiber 回顾 react-boilerplate、styled-components 等开源项目历程，并介绍其在 OpenAI 负责 ChatGPT 插件目录与平台的工作。

articles.title: Should Jensen Huang Return as Nvidia's CEO? Supporters and Critics Disagree
articles.content: "Jensen Huang is considering a comeback as Nvidia's chief executive," reports Reuters, "and has discussed with confidants the possibility of returning, the Financial Times reported on Sunday, citing people familiar with the matter." One Huang ally told the FT they were putting together a "war room" of Silicon Valley executives to lobby for the former Nvidia chief's return and would try to garner support from the White House... The report comes days after the FT reported that Nvidia's board had approached British chipmaker Arm Holdings CEO Rene Haas in its search for a potential successor to Jensen Huang. The Guardian adds that Friday two major Nvidia shareholders "urged the board to keep 'all options' open." In Washington, however, US treasury secretary Scott Bessent argued on Sunday that Nvidia should look "outside" the company for its next chief. "They need a dramatic shake-up," Bessent said on Fox News. Bessent also called on Nvidia to explain whether it knowingly allowed its most advanced AI chips to reach China, saying this was more important than Huang's affair with the alleged spy for Beijing... Bessent said he wanted answers from Nvidia and its internal investigation of Jensen Huang's behaviour within the next 10 days. The Guardian also notes Elon Musk "and a host of other tech executives are among more than 158,000 signatories of an open letter calling for Jensen Huang's reinstatement as Nvidia chief, days after he resigned from the multi-trillion dollar chip company... " The letter demands that the company's board members "bring Jensen back while an independent investigation establishes the facts"... Alongside Musk, the tech heavyweight signatories on the letter calling for Huang's return include Tim Sweeney, founder and CEO of video game publisher Epic Games, and Garry Tan, president of Y Combinator, San Francisco's most renowned business incubator. Another signatory, Uber co-founder Travis Kalanick, wrote that Huang had "erred, yes — to err is to be huma
articles.summary: 据 FT 报道，黄仁勋正考虑重返英伟达担任 CEO，并已与亲信讨论可能性，支持者与批评者意见分歧。

articles.title: FAA Router In Middle-of-nowhere Arkansas Identified as Cause of Nationwide Flight Chaos
articles.content: Though the nationwide flight-grounding ended Friday, "Nearly 2,300 flights in the U.S. have been cancelled Sunday in the aftermath..." reports ABC News. "Additionally, some 18,689 flights were delayed, per FlightAware." But "a single malfunctioning FAA router in rural Arkansas appears to have caused the air travel chaos," reports the New York Post: The problem originated at an FAA radio site in El Dorado, Arkansas, where a newly installed router flooded the network with excessive data traffic, disrupting communications between pilots and air traffic controllers, the Wall Street Journal reported. "We saw two places that were actually pinging our network at a very high rate, a thousand connections over every four to five seconds," Rebecca Guy, the FAA's technology chief, said on Saturday. .. [U.S. Transportation Secretary Sean] Duffy said the failure occurred during routine maintenance to replace aging copper telecommunications with fiber-optic cables — part of a broader effort to modernize the FAA's outdated infrastructure. The router began flooding other devices across the air traffic control network with connection attempts, disrupting both communications with aircraft and radar feeds. A radar station in Amarillo, in the Texas panhandle, is also being eyed as contributing to the outage. And new flight cancellations reported for Monday already stood at 144 as of Sunday afternoon, with 641 delayed, reports ABC News (citing data from Flight Aware): A spokesperson for Hewlett Packard Enterprise, which owns Juniper, the company that manufactured the routers believed to be central to the ground stop, said in a statement to ABC News that the devices were working properly Friday, when the ground stop occurred. "Based on what we know today, the device functioned as it was configured to by the installer. It did not fail or act improperly," the statement said... L3 Harris is a government contractor that provides technology and IT support for the Federal Aviation Administratio
articles.summary: 美国阿肯色州乡村一台 FAA 路由器故障被认定为全国航班大面积停飞的主因，周日仍有近 2300 架次取消。

articles.title: Pranksters Redirect Bitly's Links in X Posts for Trump, McDonald's and Burger King
articles.content: "A massive link-hijacking scheme has turned corporate social media archives into bizarre and offensive redirects," reports the New York Post: Posts from high-profile accounts — including fast-food giants McDonald's and Burger King, as well as President Donald Trump — are getting hacked, with over decades-old links suddenly redirecting users to unrelated website links including links about 9/11 and the Holocaust. An unknown party appears to be taking control of expired Bitly link shorteners — a widely used URL-shortening and link-management service — and altering their destinations.... Another Burger King tweet from July 13, 2011 — reading, "Now it's even easier to eat right at BURGER KING® restaurants with @WeRRestaurants. All you need is a zip code!" — was warped to link straight to Adolf Hitler's Wikipedia page... Two posts on Donald Trump's X account were also altered: a 2013 post redirected to a "Baby Fortnite" page, while a 2012 post linked to a video of Mario and Luigi from Super Mario Bros. The article notes that about 20 of Trump's old X posts had "switched" links, including some now pointing to videos of the Transformers. And it adds that "outraged web users are also slamming Bitly over its flaw that allows links to 'die' and be recycled by pranksters and bad actors." "Links dating as far back as 2009 from URL-shortening service Bitly were affected," reports CNN, "and only corporate and political X accounts appear to have been targeted, with President Donald Trump's personal account seemingly hit the hardest." "Microsoft co-founder Bill Gates, former Canadian Prime Minister Justin Trudeau and former Vice President Mike Pence... were also hit to varying degrees." Bitly said Sunday afternoon in a post on X that it had "identified an issue that allowed bad actors to repurpose certain old, inactive links to redirect people to content unrelated to the original posts." The company said it suspended the accounts that altered links and were working to disable the a
articles.summary: 恶作剧者劫持 Bitly 短链，使特朗普、麦当劳、汉堡王等账号的 X 历史帖子跳转到怪异冒犯性页面。

articles.title: Siri Glitches Ruin Reviewer's Test of Apple's New 'HomeView' Smart Speaker
articles.content: Apple has started selling its new HomeView smart speaker, a 7-inch square-with-rounded-corners screen equipped with a built-in camera. It pairs with your iPhone or iPad to offer personalized content from your email or text messages, using facial recognition to identify each family member. But in a video report, one Wall Street Journal reviewer discovered an issue while testing its smart home feature: WSJ REVIEWER: I've spent the last few years turning my home into a smart home that I can boss around with Siri. A smart lock, a special garage door opener, motorized shades, even a Raspberry Pi in my basement hooked up to my router that lets non-HomeKit devices from Ring and Nest work with Siri. It was all going well, the smart home controller of my dreams even. But then... Reviewer: Open the garage door. Siri: Sorry, I can't help with that on this device. Please use the Home app. Reviewer: Siri, you have the Home app, and you're called the HomeView. Open the garage. Siri: Sorry, I can't help with that on this device. Reviewer: Open the smart wifi garage. Siri: Sorry, I can't help with that on this device. Please use the Home app... WSJ REVIEWER: Apple explained that for security reasons, Siri won't unlock your doors or open the garage through the HomeView using voice commands. You can only tap the screen to unlock them. The concern is that someone could shout a command from outside and gain access to your house. This security concern doesn't make much sense to me. This thing can recognize my face, confirm it's me, and pull up all sorts of information from my phone. But it can't recognize me enough to open my garage? Finally I got Siri itself to explain this top-security measure. Siri: For security reasons, I can't unlock your door or open your garage from this device. Because anyone nearby can speak to a shared speaker. Reviewer: But I'm looking at you! You see my face, and you hear my voice! Siri: I understand. But I don't have a camera to see you. And voice recogniti
articles.summary: 苹果新款 HomeView 智能音箱开售，但评测中 Siri 频繁故障，影响人脸识别与个性化内容体验。

articles.title: GTA 6's Upcoming Launch Celebrated by Wendy's, YouTube, the City of Miami, and 20% of America's Workforce
articles.content: Fast food restaurant Wendy's drew an image of their redheaded mascot in the style of GTA, posting it on social media with the message "Our ride-or-dies are gonna love what we have in the works," and the date 11/19/26. That's how widespread the hype has become for Thursday's release of Grand Theft Auto VI. The BBC reports that fictional brands from the game are now actually appearing on billboards across Miami, the city that inspired the game's "Vice City" setting. And GamingBible.com reports Rockstar Games has announced Grand Theft Auto VI: The Festival, "a real-life music festival to be held in Miami, Florida... on November 21, 2026. Featuring two stages, the festival will be headlined by some incredible artists that, to state the obvious, feature on the game's soundtrack...." YouTube said pre-launch videos about the game have already racked up a whopping 40 billion views (with 900 billion views for videos about all GTA games). And now YouTube is partnering with Rockstar Games to offer several special features on launch day: Fans can drop themselves directly into Vice City using the GTAVI: Visit Vice City Shorts Effect. The feature includes multiple iconic backgrounds, making it easy for creators and fans to build their own launch-week videos... Listeners can find the official GTAVI soundtrack (featuring Morgan Wallen's "Last Thing You Need") and the complete GTA series anthology playlist directly on the YouTube Music homepage throughout launch week... Starting November 19 at 12 AM ET, fans worldwide can tune in to youtube.com/youtube for a 24 hour stream packed with live gameplay, creator podcasts, and original content featuring top creators... [On launch day] fans can jump straight into the global broadcast by clicking the custom GTAVI-themed YouTube logo (Yoodle) on the YouTube homepage At one one study suggests nearly one in a five U.S. workers plan to skip work on Thursday, writes the New York Post: Roughly 18% of workers plan to take Thursday off to park them
articles.summary: 《GTA 6》发售引发全民热潮，Wendy's、YouTube、迈阿密市及约两成美国劳动力以各种方式参与造势。

articles.title: Huawei Set To Challenge Tesla Powerwall with New, 20 kW Home Battery
articles.content: "Huawei believes its new Luterra S2 is more than just a home backup battery," reports Electrek: This high-tech Huawei home battery pack hopes to hold back Tesla's latest Powerwall with silicon carbide technology, AI-powered energy management baked in, and enough modular storage to keep even large homes bright and warm when the rest of the block goes dark... The Chinese tech firm is calling it an "all-in-one residential energy system" that combines a hybrid inverter, modular battery storage, and AI-powered energy management in a single, simple, and stackable package that's available in single-phase versions that put out between 3 and 10 kW and three-phase versions that can push up to 20 kW. The Luterra S2 is the first system of its kind to use Huawei's proprietary full-silicon carbide (SiC) architecture, which promises improved efficiency, power density, and ease of use. It's so easy, in fact, that Huawei claims it can be installed and commissioned in just minutes. Huawei's basic Luterra S2 configuration starts with "just" 5 kWh of battery energy storage and 3 kW of output. That's enough to keep essential household appliances, lighting, and electronics running during a power outage, but you'll want to keep going if you're preparing for more than a day or two without power. If that sounds like you, Luterra's got you covered. The modular system can be expanded with modular 7 kWh LFP battery packs and can keep scaling up to a massive 336 kWh of total storage across interconnected systems, with inverter output peaking at an impressive 60 kW using three 20 kW units in parallel. Keeping all that power cool and quiet is a Huawei-developed passive cooling system that does without external fans, keeping operating noise levels below a claimed 29 dB (about the same as my Mac mini). Read more of this story at Slashdot.
articles.summary: 华为推出 20kW 家用电池 Luterra S2，采用碳化硅与 AI 能源管理，直接挑战特斯拉 Powerwall。

articles.title: Bill Gates Has Earned Billions Investing in Climate-Polluting Landfills, Reports ProPublica
articles.content: Environmental activist Bill Gates has "quietly accumulated a $29 billion stake in America's No. 2 landfill operator, Republic Services," reports ProPublica, in a new 5,000-word investigation. But inspectors from America's Environmental Protection Agency "have repeatedly found methane — a highly potent greenhouse gas — escaping from Republic landfills at levels above federal limits. Republic has lobbied against regulations that could make the waste industry cleaner, including by keeping organic garbage out of landfills in the first place." While Gates has invested at least $2 billion in green companies, he's "put more than double that amount into a very dirty, old-school industry," their article argues. And Gates has increased his stake in Republic "to 38% of the company, a position worth $29 billion." While fossil fuels get most of the attention, scientists increasingly see landfills as a crucial climate issue. They're responsible for as much as a fifth of the country's emissions of methane, a highly potent greenhouse gas, studies show. Republic alone generates as much climate pollution as 3 million gasoline-burning cars each year, according to its own reports.... [Gates] has failed to make Republic live up to his own climate principles, a ProPublica investigation has found. Federal inspectors have repeatedly found methane escaping from Republic landfills at levels above federal limits. The company has refrained from adopting the ambitious emissions-reduction goal embraced by its main competitor... "It seems very likely that Bill Gates has the power to influence Republic's behavior to make it more climate-friendly, even if that costs the company profits," said Ann Lipton, a legal scholar who studies corporate governance at the University of Colorado, Boulder... Gates didn't respond to repeated requests to discuss his landfill investments, and ProPublica couldn't find any public comments he's made about them. But the bet has proven wildly lucrative. articles.content: "In November's edition of the TIOBE Index, Rust has dropped out of Top 10," writes I-Programmer, noting that Rust ceded the #10 position to Go. "At the same time, another Google-originated language, Dart, has entered the top 20 ousting Julia after only one month." TIOBE explains Dart's popularity is mainly being driven by Flutter, Google's framework for building cross-platform mobile applications. In fact, Flutter has become one of the major technologies for cross-platform mobile app development. The Dart language itself is not particularly unique, although it incorporates many modern programming language features. Its success is largely driven by the strength of the Flutter ecosystem and the convenience of developing applications for multiple platforms using a single codebase... [In November's ranking] Visual Basic has also lost two places, making room for R and SQL in the Top 10. Further down the ranking, Assembly has re-entered the Top 20.
